newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to buy sugar at 610-650 pesos per 50kg.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to buy sugar at 610-650 pesos per 50kg.

text.p: Philippine Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said on Tuesday he had ordered the National Food Authority (NFA) to buy raw sugar from farmers at between 610 and 650 pesos per 50 kg bag starting this week.
The NFA is targetting to buy 200,000 tonnes of sugar.
Domestic sugar prices dropped to 560 to 576 pesos per bag last week. Farmers say the average prouction cost of sugar is 627 pesos per bag.
Escudero said in a statement the buying programme was just a "temporary bail-out" and would last until June 30 this year unless extended by the government.

"I would like to appeal to the people in the industry to address the medium and long-term solutions so there won't be a repetition of this drop in price," he told sugar farmers in the central city of Bacolod, in Negros Occidental province.
The government recently set up a four billion peso Sugar Procurement Fund which would be funded from a credit line extended by the Philippine National Bank.
Negros Occidental governor Rafael Coscolluela said he expected domestic sugar prices to stabilise because of the government procurement programme.
